CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. To identify an instrument we give its name, its community and (1 mark)
   A. the name of the shop
   B. how it is played
   C. the colour of the shop
   D. its price

2. Which of these is a dark tone of red? (1 mark)
   A. Red mixed with water
   B. Red mixed with a little black
   C. Red mixed with yellow
   D. Red mixed with white

3. In ta-te taa taa (rest), how many beats are there? (1 mark)
   A. Five
   B. Three
   C. Four
   D. Two

4. Rhythm is (1 mark)
   A. the pattern of long and short sounds
   B. the loudness of the singer
   C. the name of the song
   D. how high a note is

5. A pair of quavers together lasts (1 mark)
   A. one beat
   B. two beats
   C. half a beat
   D. four beats

6. Which of these four-beat patterns ends on a long note? (1 mark)
   A. ta-te taa ta-te taa
   B. ta-te ta-te ta-te ta-te
   C. taa taa taa (rest)
   D. taa ta-te taa (rest)

7. What is clay? (1 mark)
   A. Fine sticky soil that is soft when wet and hard when dry
   B. A kind of wood
   C. A metal
   D. A type of paper

8. How can you make a slab of even thickness? (1 mark)
   A. Roll the clay with a bottle between two sticks of equal thickness
   B. Squeeze with one hand
   C. Freeze it
   D. Drop it on the floor

9. Before joining a coil to a slab you should (1 mark)
   A. cover with oil
   B. scratch both and dab a little water
   C. paint them
   D. dry them in the sun

10. What is the first command at the start of a race? (1 mark)
   A. Set
   B. On your marks
   C. Go
   D. Stop

11. Which is a good ratio of length to height for a flag drawing? (1 mark)
   A. Ten to one
   B. One to one
   C. Two to three tall
   D. Three to two

12. Why is the national flag flown at national athletics events? (1 mark)
   A. To hide the track
   B. To decorate only
   C. It shows which country the athletes represent and builds pride
   D. To block the wind

13. Which part of the foot should touch the ground when sprinting? (1 mark)
   A. The ankle
   B. The heel
   C. The front part of the foot
   D. The side only

14. What should you do with long hair in gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. Tie it back
   B. Cut it during class
   C. Cover the mat with it
   D. Let it hang in your face

15. How can you fix sagging hips in the crab balance? (1 mark)
   A. Push harder through your hands and feet
   B. Bend your arms
   C. Drop your head
   D. Lie down

16. In a side roll, you should keep your legs (1 mark)
   A. wide apart
   B. together with toes pointed
   C. bent
   D. lifted off the mat

17. Why should you sing folk songs from other communities with respect? (1 mark)
   A. They are unimportant
   B. They must be changed
   C. They are funny
   D. They are part of our shared culture

18. Which folk songs are sung when young people become adults in their community? (1 mark)
   A. Work songs
   B. Initiation songs
   C. Naming songs
   D. Topical songs

19. What is the danger of pointing a camera directly at the sun? (1 mark)
   A. It saves the battery
   B. It can hurt your eyes and spoil the picture
   C. It makes the picture sharper
   D. It makes the sun cooler

20. Which light is best for outdoor photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Darkness
   B. A torch in the eyes
   C. Only midday shadows
   D. Natural sunlight falling on the subject

21. Which of these can also take digital photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Drum
   B. Xylophone
   C. Tablet
   D. Broom

22. Which part of the finger covers a hole? (1 mark)
   A. The fingertip edge
   B. The nail
   C. The soft pad
   D. The knuckle

23. Which note is played with the thumb and holes 1 and 2 covered? (1 mark)
   A. D
   B. B
   C. A
   D. G

24. Why is it called the mushroom float? (1 mark)
   A. It grows
   B. It is very tall
   C. It tastes good
   D. The back at the surface looks like the top of a mushroom

25. You begin a glide by (1 mark)
   A. pushing gently off the wall
   B. kicking the wall in anger
   C. jumping from a height
   D. swimming hard

26. In the hawk and the chicks game, the chicks (1 mark)
   A. run away
   B. hold on gently behind the hen
   C. sing
   D. hit the hawk

27. To analyse a work of art means to (1 mark)
   A. throw it away
   B. look closely at its parts to understand it
   C. ignore it
   D. paint over it

28. The Kenya National Anthem is a (1 mark)
   A. a game
   B. a topical song about washing
   C. a work song
   D. national symbol

29. Two stars and a wish means (1 mark)
   A. two songs and a wish
   B. two mistakes and a prize
   C. two lines and a circle
   D. two good comments and one suggestion

30. What should be written on the portfolio label? (1 mark)
   A. Nothing
   B. The price
   C. A secret
   D. Your name, class and title

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain how you would learn a simple melody on B, A and G. (4 marks)

32. Explain why animal games are called indigenous activities. (3 marks)

33. Why is gymnastics not a race? (2 marks)

34. What is a false start? (2 marks)

35. Describe how to make a montage on ball games. (4 marks)

36. Explain what sportsmanship means and give two examples. (3 marks)

37. Describe the steps of modelling the letters d, r and m on clay slabs. (5 marks)

38. Explain why only the Goal Shooter and Goal Attack can score goals. (3 marks)

39. Explain how to tie an overhand knot. (3 marks)

40. Describe the roles of the soloist, the chorus and the instrumentalists in a folk song. (3 marks)

41. What does it mean to appreciate a work of Creative Arts? (2 marks)

42. Explain how animal games help to keep the body healthy. (4 marks)

43. Explain how to take a portrait of a friend with good light and a clear centre of interest. (5 marks)

44. When is an overhead pass better than a chest pass? (2 marks)

45. How should clay models be dried and why? (2 marks)

46. How do you care for a paint brush? (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — MOCK EXAM #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — how it is played
   Identifying uses name, community and method of playing.

2. B — Red mixed with a little black
   Adding black makes a darker shade of red.

3. C — Four
   Each of ta-te, taa, taa and the rest fills one beat, so there are four beats.

4. A — the pattern of long and short sounds
   Rhythm is the pattern of sounds over the beat.

5. A — one beat
   Two half beats make one whole beat.

6. A — ta-te taa ta-te taa
   Only the first ends on a crotchet (taa).

7. A — Fine sticky soil that is soft when wet and hard when dry
   Clay is a fine, sticky soil used for modelling.

8. A — Roll the clay with a bottle between two sticks of equal thickness
   Equal sticks on both sides keep the slab even.

9. B — scratch both and dab a little water
   Scratching and wetting help the clay pieces stick.

10. B — On your marks
   The starter first says on your marks.

11. D — Three to two
   A flag rectangle is about one and a half times as long as it is high.

12. C — It shows which country the athletes represent and builds pride
   The flag is a symbol of the country.

13. C — The front part of the foot
   Sprinters land on the balls of the feet.

14. A — Tie it back
   Tied-back hair does not get in your way.

15. A — Push harder through your hands and feet
   Pushing through hands and feet lifts the hips.

16. B — together with toes pointed
   Legs stay together to keep the log shape.

17. D — They are part of our shared culture
   Respect helps unity and cultural appreciation.

18. B — Initiation songs
   Initiation songs mark the change from child to adult.

19. B — It can hurt your eyes and spoil the picture
   Looking at the sun harms the eyes.

20. D — Natural sunlight falling on the subject
   Natural light is best.

21. C — Tablet
   Many tablets have cameras.

22. C — The soft pad
   Pads seal the hole fully.

23. C — A
   A uses thumb, 1 and 2.

24. D — The back at the surface looks like the top of a mushroom
   The rounded back at the top looks like a mushroom cap.

25. A — pushing gently off the wall
   A gentle push is enough.

26. B — hold on gently behind the hen
   Chicks stay in line.

27. B — look closely at its parts to understand it
   Analysing means studying the parts.

28. D — national symbol
   Like the flag, it stands for the nation.

29. D — two good comments and one suggestion
   Give two positives and one idea to improve.

30. D — Your name, class and title
   A label shows whose portfolio it is.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sing it in sol-fa, clap and say the rhythm, finger the notes without blowing, play slowly, then speed up keeping the beat steady.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: They come from the communities and their environment, need little or no equipment and are learnt by watching and joining in.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is about control and quality of movement, not about speed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for control, 1 mark for not speed.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: Leaving the start line before the last signal is given.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for leaving early, 1 mark for before the signal.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: Collect and cut pictures of ball games from old papers. Arrange them on a background without gluing, overlapping the pieces. Paste the back ones first and then the others. Add a title and let it dry.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Being fair and kind in sports. Examples: following the rules and shaking hands with the other team.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for each example.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: Prepare and knead clay. Roll a slab and cut three rectangles of different sizes. Make coils. Shape a coil into each letter and scratch and wet where they join. Press on gently, smooth, and let dry slowly in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for preparing clay, cutting slabs, making coils, joining, and drying.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Netball rules say only these two attackers may shoot, and only from inside the goal circle. Other players help by passing the ball to them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the two players, 1 mark for the goal circle, 1 mark for the role of the others.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Make a loop with the cord. Pass the end through the loop. Pull both ends to tighten.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: The soloist leads, the chorus answers and repeats, the instrumentalists play instruments to keep the beat.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each role.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: To notice, understand and value it, giving reasons for what you think.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: They strengthen muscles, stretch the body, improve balance and coordination and make the heart and lungs stronger.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: Ask permission. Put the sun behind you so light falls on the friend's face. Choose a plain background. Move closer so the face fills the picture. Hold the device steadily, press gently and check the photograph.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five points.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: When a defender stands close so that the ball must go over their arms.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a defender, 1 mark for going over.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Slowly in the shade. Strong sun dries them too fast and makes them crack.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rinse when changing colour, wash with soap after use, shape the tip and store it flat or with hairs up. Never leave it standing on its hairs in water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point.
